why: reviewer (minor): Root labelled only as √dhā; the printed verb is vi-√dhā (the prefix vi- is part of vidhīyate).

old: These are the fruits of the tree of one's own fault for embodied beings: poverty, sorrow, diseases, bondage and calamities.
new: These are the fruits of the tree of one's own fault, of embodied beings: poverty, sorrow, diseases, bondage and calamities.
why: reviewer (minor): dehinām is genitive (of embodied beings); 'for' gives it a dative sense the Sanskrit does not carry (gram and Hindi correctly keep the genitive).

old: Indeed, the union of many beings is enemy-conquering; the cloud that bears streams of rain is warded off even by straws.
new: And indeed, the union of many beings is enemy-conquering; the cloud that bears streams of rain is warded off even by straws.
why: reviewer (minor): The printed ca of caiva is dropped: the draft keeps only 'indeed' for eva although its own word split glosses ca as 'and'. Unit 17 renders the same ca eva as 'and indeed'; the glossary rule is that a printed ca appears in both languages.

old: प्राणियों के बहुतों का मेल ही शत्रुओं को जीतने वाला है; वर्षा की धाराओं को धारण करने वाला मेघ तिनकों से भी रोका जाता है।
new: और बहुत-से प्राणियों का मेल निश्चय ही शत्रुओं को जीतने वाला है; वर्षा की धाराओं को धारण करने वाला मेघ तिनकों से भी रोका जाता है।
why: reviewer (minor): Garbled rendering of bahūnāṃ sattvānām ('of many beings'): 'of the many of the beings' is not what the Sanskrit says. The printed ca is also dropped in Hindi.

old: ca eva rendered together as emphatic 'indeed' (no coordinate partner for ca). ripuñjaya taken as an adjective 'enemy-conquering'.
new: ca eva rendered 'and indeed'; ca has no coordinate partner in the verse. ripuñjaya taken as an adjective 'enemy-conquering'.
why: reviewer (minor): Note records the dropped ca as a choice; it should now describe the corrected rendering.
reviewer (minor): nivāryate is the passive of the causative stem (nivārayati), not of the simple root; the label omits caus.

old: The mind that comes to be in the exposition of dharma and in the cremation ground, and that of the sick: if that should remain always indeed, who would not be freed from bondage?
new: The mind that may come to be in the exposition of dharma and in the cremation ground, of the sick: if that should remain always indeed, who would not be freed from bondage?
why: reviewer (error): Adds a second 'and': the Sanskrit has one ca, after śmaśāne; rogiṇām follows with no connective. Also bhavet is optative ('may come to be'), not a plain present.

old: धर्म के कथन में और श्मशान में, और रोगियों की जो बुद्धि होती है, वह यदि सदा ही बनी रहे, कौन बन्धन से मुक्त न हो जाए?
new: धर्म के कथन में और श्मशान में रोगियों की जो बुद्धि हो, वह यदि सदा ही बनी रहे, कौन बन्धन से मुक्त न हो जाए?
why: reviewer (error): Second 'और' is not in the Sanskrit (one ca only), and the optative bhavet is rendered as a plain present (होती है); the glossary keeps the optative in Hindi.

old: tu is weak here and left untranslated. tasya brūyāt: genitive of the person addressed, rendered 'to him'.
new: tu is weak here and left untranslated. tasya brūyāt: genitive of the person addressed, rendered 'to him'. susvaram may also be an adjective agreeing with gītam ('a sweet-toned song'); the adverbial reading is taken here.
why: reviewer (minor): Neuter accusative susvaram stands beside gītam and can equally be an adjective of the song ('a sweet-toned song'); the draft fixes the adverbial reading without saying the other is open, and 'sweet-voiced' in the English reads as describing the hunter.

old: The feminine āsannā, dūrasthā, phalapradā in line a have no expressed subject; they agree with striyaḥ or an implied feminine noun, and line a is taken as applying to the four of line b. madhya-bhāva = a middle attitude, i.e. moderation.
new: The feminine āsannā, dūrasthā, phalapradā in line a have no expressed subject; they agree with an implied feminine noun that the line does not state. madhya-bhāva = a middle attitude, i.e. moderation.
why: reviewer (minor): Unsupported: nothing in the Sanskrit links line a to the four subjects of line b, and agreement with striyaḥ is not shown (striyaḥ is plural, the adjectives singular). The note presents an interpretation as the reading.

old: He lives whose are virtues; he lives whose is dharma. For one devoid of virtue and dharma, life is purposeless.
new: He lives whose are virtues; he lives whose is dharma. Of one devoid of virtue and dharma, life is purposeless.
why: reviewer (minor): Sentence-initial 'For' reads as a causal connective the Sanskrit lacks; the genitive guṇa-dharma-vihīnasya stands with no particle.
reviewer (minor): nivāraya is the causative stem of ni-√vṛ; label omits caus.

old: कोयलों द्वारा भी दिन तब तक मौन में बिताए जाते हैं, जब तक सब लोगों को आनन्द देने वाली वाणी प्रवृत्त नहीं होती।
new: कोयलों द्वारा और निश्चय ही दिन तब तक मौन में बिताए जाते हैं, जब तक सब लोगों को आनन्द देने वाली वाणी प्रवृत्त नहीं होती।
why: reviewer (error): भी is used for the printed ca (ca eva); glossary: ca = and (और), never 'too/also/भी', which is reserved for api. No api is printed here.

old: Days are passed in silence by cuckoos indeed, until speech giving joy to all people goes forth.
new: Days are passed in silence by cuckoos, and indeed,, until speech giving joy to all people goes forth.
why: reviewer (minor): The printed ca is dropped in English (only eva is rendered), though the word split glosses ca as 'and'.

old: tāvat ... yāvat with a present verb is taken as 'up to the time that / until'; the Hindi uses the idiomatic negative. ca eva is rendered as emphatic 'indeed'.
new: tāvat ... yāvat with a present verb is taken as 'up to the time that / until'; the Hindi uses the idiomatic negative. ca eva is rendered 'and indeed'; ca has no coordinate partner.
why: reviewer (minor): Note must match the corrected rendering.
